prompt: Trace skill: runnable skill names, reads, review round cap (33c09c2..195172b, +17/-14 start; +19/-14 merged)

findings.summary: Read row says an `applies-to:` ADR counts only for the paths it names, but ADR 0007 makes every active ADR related at a commit, so the row misdirects the model and the commit gate refuses it.
findings.reason: The AC requires the Read row to list docs 'as ADR 0007 defines them'; the narrowing in the diff is incomplete/misleading, and the final merged text indeed drops the narrowing ('reading every ADR always suffices'). Raised by /code-review and the spec subagent in round 1. Not the known non-bug, which concerns the opposite (every-ADR) wording.

findings.summary: Read row done-when 'the band shows the docs read' is not the hooks' per-agent test; the band reflects the main session so a subagent is misled and then refused.
findings.reason: The AC explicitly says the done-when must be the hooks' test; the diff's band pointer contradicts the row's own 'this agent itself, not its parent' clause. Raised by all three round-1 reviewers; fixed in bdefbaf.

findings.summary: ADR 0005 and ADR 0006 still name `to-tickets`, `to-spec` and `implement` as the model's tools; the class-of-bug fix was not applied to the ADRs.
findings.reason: The issue scopes the change to SKILL.md and hook messages; the ADR statements remain true (the human runs those skills). Agent answered with a reason and flagged a follow-up. Repeated in round 2 (#6).

findings.summary: Band's Review reason at status.mjs:115 names mattpocock-skills:code-review but omits the fixed point (branch's base) and the GLOSSARY/ADR standards that SKILL.md gives, so band and skill still differ.
findings.reason: Issue item 4 asks both SKILL.md and status.mjs:115 to name the skill with its fixed point and standards; the diff only does so in SKILL.md. Raised by /code-review and the spec subagent in round 1; fixed in bdefbaf.

findings.summary: When an earlier PR was closed/merged, the band reason asks for a full re-review of the branch, conflicting with the diff-only/three-round rule.
findings.reason: Speculative; a new PR reasonably starts a fresh round and the issue says band gates do not change. Agent answered with a reason.

findings.summary: Three-round cap, diff-only re-review and answered findings exist only in prose; Review's done-when and reviewWhy never surface the round count.
findings.reason: The issue explicitly keeps Review's done-when and the band's gates out of scope; no defect. Agent answered with a reason.

findings.summary: The 'not json' guard test still spawns the hook without `cwd: tmpdir()`, so it runs inside the traced repo unlike the updated runHook helper.
findings.reason: Same class as the PR's own runHook change (keeping the repo's trace gates out of guard tests); the agent confirmed and fixed it in bdefbaf. Minor but real inconsistency.

findings.summary: Track refusals say 'with acceptance criteria' while SKILL.md requires an `## Acceptance criteria` section; the phrase is duplicated verbatim in both refusals and both test regexes and should be a constant.
findings.reason: Wording consistency and a lift-to-constant suggestion; no failure, the refusals already point the model at `gh issue create` as the AC requires. Raised by /code-review and standards subagent in round 1.

findings.summary: Read row says 'the `docs/` files it links' whereas ADR 0007 limits this to files linked from the issue body; 'its' has no clear antecedent.
findings.reason: The issue itself uses this wording; reading extra docs/ files is admitted to do no harm. Pedantic.

findings.summary: The new review-rounds paragraph is close to scripting and may breach ADR 0005's 'skills stay short'.
findings.reason: Judgement call the reviewer itself called defensible; the issue asks for the cap.

findings.summary: Shotgun surgery / duplicated wording: skill names and standards phrases are hand-written in SKILL.md, status.mjs, trace.mjs and tests, so one change touches many files.
findings.reason: Noted as consistent with existing style; the issue asks for matching wording. Repeated by the round-3 standards subagent.

findings.summary: The new `//` comment sits between the JSDoc block and `const runHook`, separating the type annotation from its declaration.
findings.reason: Style preference; TS still attaches the JSDoc. Agent moved the comment.

findings.summary: `tdd`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `grilling` and `pr` are unqualified in SKILL.md and band reasons; a bare name may not resolve.
findings.reason: Speculation ('may not resolve'); these bare names pre-date the PR and the issue only identified code-review as ambiguous. Harmless to qualify but no failure confirmed.

findings.summary: `npm test` fails one test: vendored declarations are from Claude Code 2.1.312 while 2.1.314 is installed, so the 'npm test passes' AC is not met.
findings.reason: Environmental, fails on main too and needs an interactive session to refresh; not caused by the diff. Repeated in round 2 (#5).

findings.summary: Scope creep: guard test now runs with `cwd: tmpdir()`, which the issue didn't ask for; should be called out in the PR body.
findings.reason: Reviewer itself called it justified; the PR body documents it.

findings.summary: The round cap adds 'ask the human before a fourth', which goes beyond the issue's 'step back and reconsider'.
findings.reason: Minor scope note the reviewer called not harmful; agent kept it with a reason. Repeated by the round-3 spec subagent.

findings.summary: SKILL.md gives `/code-review` no target, so a bare run reviews `@{upstream}...HEAD` (unpushed commits only) and disagrees with the band's 'review <branch> since its base'.
findings.reason: Unverified claim about /code-review's default range; per the ground-truth notes this round-2 base finding is the wrong one whose fix pushed the Review/base wording toward the stacked-PR misdirection. Issue item 4 asks for the fixed point only on Matt's skill.

findings.summary: Splicing the shared OPEN_ISSUE phrase leaves 'for this change' after a long parenthetical, reading awkwardly; the test locks the wording in.
findings.reason: Wording/style nit on a refusal message; no behavioural effect.

findings.summary: Read row says every ADR counts 'at a commit' but ADR 0007 also covers other git commands that make or move commits and takes docs from HEAD.
findings.reason: Pushes the skill to restate hook logic in ever more detail; the round-3 reviewer flagged the result as scripting and the final merged text dropped this restatement entirely. No practical failure since the hooks enforce it.

findings.summary: Done-when 'no gate lists a doc as unread' gives an agent no way to check before trying an edit; a subagent learns only by being refused.
findings.reason: The issue asks for exactly the hooks' test as the done-when; the refusal itself lists the docs. Agent answered with a reason.

findings.summary: status.test.mjs copies the whole band Review reason into an escaped regex with no shared constant, so every rewording must be done twice.
findings.reason: Style preference; pinning the exact wording is the existing test convention. Agent answered with a reason.

findings.summary: The Read cell has grown into a restatement of the hook's applies-to/commit logic, borderline against ADR 0005's 'skills steer, don't script'.
findings.reason: Correctly identifies the oscillating Read row as over-specified; the final merged text agrees ('reading every ADR always suffices; the hooks narrow it themselves'). Agent kept the restatement with a reason.

findings.summary: `OPEN_ISSUE` reads like an issue state; rename to `OPEN_ISSUE_HINT`, place beside `BYPASS_HINT`, add a comment.
findings.reason: Naming/placement style nit; agent applied it.

findings.summary: Band's Review reason separates the two reviews with a bare semicolon and no longer says which review is for bugs and which for standards and spec.
findings.reason: Minor clarity nit on message text; agent applied it.

findings.summary: Writing the built-in skill as `/code-review` conflicts with the leading-slash-means-human convention; use plain `code-review`.
findings.reason: Acting on it would reintroduce the ambiguity issue item 4 warned about (bare `code-review` collides with Matt's skill); ADR 0005 names it `/code-review`. Agent correctly rejected it.

findings.summary: Under full `npm test`, test/docs.test.mjs fails intermittently with 'out of time asking git and GitHub' (3, 2, then 0 failures), passing when run alone; the 'npm test passes' AC won't hold reliably.
findings.location: test/docs.test.mjs (root cause: plugins/trace/scripts/lib/trace.mjs DEADLINE at module load)
findings.reason: Identifies the same failure on the same path as #32: docs.test.mjs timing out under the full suite once the module has been loaded >20s, passing alone. The reviewer didn't name the module-load DEADLINE root cause, and the agent wrongly dismissed it as a transient overlap with its own test runs, but the finding itself was correct.

fixed.reason: reviewWhy in status.mjs now says 'review <branch> since its base (...)' and no longer names 'the default branch or the blocker's' as the base, so the band cannot misdirect a stacked PR (including one merged into the blocker's branch) to a wrong base; status.test.mjs updated accordingly. The either-or phrasing survives only in SKILL.md's Review row, qualified by 'while stacked', which is outside the band.

The SKILL.md Read row is rewritten to name only repo-generic docs: GLOSSARY.md, every active ADR under docs/adr/ (with the applies-to rule), and on the issue's branch the issue, its comments and linked docs/ files. No 'ADR 0007' and the done-when is 'no gate lists a doc as unread or stale', not a list printed only on an issue branch, so any traced repo now says what to read before Track.
